topic: Full-outcome detector symmetrization with reference-free scalar efficiency and dark-rate acquisition
overall_status: An exact cyclic M-setting permutation reduces stable heterogeneous detector efficiencies and Poisson dark rates to a common iid row law for the completed Gaussian-block instrument. An independent anytime source-on/source-off pilot selects a fixed main dose from acquired lower/upper confidence bounds. The averaging operation itself is established QKD prior art; exact detector hardware, coefficient calibration, source flux, drift transfer, and fixed-N randomized schedule remain physical gates.

claims.statement: For a complete M-outcome POVM {E_j}, stable detector efficiencies eta_i and independent dark rates b_i, equal-duration cyclic assignment pi_s(j)=j+s mod M over all s=0,...,M-1, and independent Poisson launch flux phi, the aggregate row counts are independent Pois(N eta_bar p_j(x)+beta), where eta_bar=M^{-1}sum_i eta_i, beta=T b_bar, N=phi T, and p_j=x*E_j x. The total source-click count is Pois(N eta_bar) for every unit x. An independent source-off cycle of duration rT gives independent row blanks Pois(r beta). The statement includes all residual outcomes and needs uniform exposure and detector-only scalar response.
assumptions: The frame is a known complete M-outcome POVM and every outcome, including residual ports, is measured during each complete cycle.
Every detector response is a stable scalar efficiency in [0,1] plus an independent Poisson dark process with stable rate.
Source flux and prepared state are constant during each equal-duration cycle; source launches are Poissonized in the reference experiment.
Permutation controls are lossless and do not change state, mode-dependent response, or detector gating; no dead time, afterpulsing, or saturation occurs.
claims.status: Exact internally derived count-law reduction; finite rational fixture checked in symmetrization_check.py. Hardware validity is untested.
claims.novelty_boundary: Detector symmetrization/randomization is prior art in QKD. No novelty claim for permutation averaging; the narrow claim is the exact all-outcome iid Poisson reduction and its use for reference-free scalar acquisition in this completed tomography interface.
claims.costs: M settings per signal cycle and M per row-resolved blank; N expected launched photons, residual/loss events included; source flux monitor, frame coefficients, switch time, blank time, and all dark events are separately charged.
claims.falsifier: State-dependent total source yield under a complete cycle, unequal row backgrounds after blank cycling, or setting-dependent detector response / flux / mode loss outside the model.

claims.statement: For a fixed M-outcome POVM and generic state pair x,y with all outcome probabilities positive, choose any c<=min_j{p_j(x),p_j(y)} and detector efficiencies eta_j=c/p_j(x), eta'_j=c/p_j(y). Both vectors lie in [0,1]^M and make every Poissonized fixed-setting source-channel mean equal Nc under the two different states. Thus arbitrary unknown static per-channel efficiencies obstruct uniform no-reference state recovery even with zero background; cyclic completion removes this specific confound by giving row means eta_bar p_j and a state-independent all-port click total.
assumptions: Every outcome probability of both selected states is strictly positive.
The nuisance class allows world-dependent unknown efficiencies in [0,1]^M.
Source-only Poisson counts are compared under one fixed detector assignment; no independent reference probes are supplied.
claims.status: Exact two-state construction internally derived; it does not cover restricted efficiency ranges or calibrated references.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary nuisance nonidentifiability, not a new phase-retrieval result. A related arbitrary-channel dark-count obstruction is in the inherited measurement_inverse CYCLE3 report.
claims.costs: No recovery guarantee is possible for this unrestricted nuisance class from the stated fixed-setting source counts alone.
claims.falsifier: An additional restriction/reference that rules out the constructed efficiency vectors or separates source yields.

claims.statement: With calibrated launched flux phi, stable parameters eta_bar>0 and Gamma=sum_i b_i, cumulative independent source-on/off total counts over equal exposure t have rates u=phi eta_bar+Gamma and v=Gamma. Per-look exact Garwood intervals with alpha-spending delta_l=3 alpha/(pi^2(l+1)^2) yield simultaneous time-uniform coverage at least 1-alpha. The stopping conditions eta_L>0, eta_U<=2 eta_L, and Gamma_U<=2 Gamma_L+phi eta_L imply eta_L>=eta_bar/2 and Gamma_U<=2 Gamma+phi eta_bar on the coverage event. The stop is almost surely finite. Pilot launched photons scale, up to constants and a log-log anytime factor, as (phi eta_bar+2Gamma)/(phi eta_bar^2); off exposure of equal duration and M on-settings per cycle are additional costs.
assumptions: The complete source-on detector cycle makes its total source-click mean state-independent.
Source flux phi and the launch denominator are known from independent calibrated flux metrology or heralding; otherwise phi eta_bar is not separated.
Source-on and source-off total counts are independent Poisson processes with rates u and v, and detector parameters remain stable from pilot to main acquisition.
The pilot is independent of fresh main signal and main blank records, and no main-record stopping is used.
claims.status: Confidence sequence and rate calculations internally derived; exact interval construction is standard. Finite-sample physical validation is absent.
claims.novelty_boundary: The state-independent calibration observable and anytime stopping are a composition with established Poisson inference, not detector-efficiency symmetrization prior art itself. Priority for this exact combined protocol remains unknown.
claims.costs: Pilot photons, source-off detector time and dark events, calibrated flux, M on-settings per cycle, one static off setting for scalar dark-rate monitoring, plus a separate fresh main blank.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the total-count state invariance or invalid Poisson/stability/flux assumptions; in particular unknown flux leaves an efficiency-flux gauge.

claims.statement: On the simultaneous pilot coverage event, choosing a fixed fresh main dose N>=C[d/(eta_L epsilon^2)+dm Gamma_U/(M phi eta_L^2 epsilon^2)] and an independent rowwise blank of relative duration r=1 reduces the stable heterogeneous detector model exactly to the Cycle 3 common-background HLN Theorem 4 model on its iid Gaussian block. For m=Theta(d), this suffices at order d/(eta_bar epsilon^2)+d Gamma/(phi eta_bar^2 epsilon^2), including all launched photons and independent blank dark counts. The estimator uses only the first m Gaussian rows; residual rows remain physically measured for symmetrization.
assumptions: Cycle 3 HLN Theorem 4 hypotheses and its hidden constants, oversampling, high-energy and normalization conditions hold.
The detector/flux/frame assumptions of C4-EXACT-CYCLIC-POISSON-REDUCTION hold between pilot, main signal and independent blank.
The dose is selected only from the independent pilot; the main signal dose is fixed before its rows are observed.
The independent blank has the same duration/symmetrization schedule as the main signal and is not reused from pilot data.
claims.status: Internally derived sufficient composition with prior HLN Theorem 4; no end-to-end hardware or numerical solver guarantee.
claims.novelty_boundary: The O(d/epsilon^2) rate and estimator are established prior art. The new interface claim is conditional exact treatment of unknown stable per-detector response plus acquired scalar bounds; detector symmetrization as an idea is prior art.
claims.costs: N main photons plus pilot photons; residual/loss outcomes; independent r=1 blank with expected T Gamma total dark events; M main and M blank settings; O(md)=O(d^2) known frame coefficients and optical synthesis remain separate.
claims.falsifier: Any failure of the iid row law, blank independence/equal mean, pilot-to-main stability, source flux calibration, or the inherited HLN transfer assumptions.

claims.statement: For the M-window Poisson reference with independent launch totals Pois(N/M), conditioning only on their global total N makes window allocations Multinomial(N;1/M,...,1/M), equal to a fixed-N source that assigns each photon an independent uniform setting label and batches by equal-duration windows. Full source click/loss outcomes are multinomial with marginalized detected row probability eta_bar p_j; independent full-window dark processes and an independent blank are unchanged by conditioning. Any aggregate-record failure probability transfers with one factor 1/P(Pois(N)=N)=O(sqrt(N)), independent of M. This does not apply to deterministic balanced per-window quotas.
assumptions: The fixed-N protocol randomizes photon setting labels uniformly; it does not force exactly N/M photons in each setting.
Every detector remains active over fixed equal-duration windows; dark counts are independent of source allocation and do not depend on flux or detector history.
The estimator event depends on aggregated rows and independent blank; all source loss/no-click outcomes are included in the latent global total.
Pilot and main are independent; the fixed-N main dose is selected before its counts.
claims.status: Exact conditioning identity internally derived and finite categorical algebra checked. Randomized timing/flux protocol is not physically validated.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary Poisson-multinomial conditioning; no new concentration theorem. Deterministic quota schedules and detector gating are outside the proof.
claims.costs: One O(sqrt(N)) tail factor, N fixed launches, M equal-time windows, random source scheduling, continuous detector exposure and deadtime/saturation validation.
claims.falsifier: A mismatch between random-window fixed-N allocations and the conditional Poisson source model, or any coupling of detector dark events/gating to the allocation.

claims.statement: Within a control class that mixes port-permutation matrices with nonnegative exposure weights, exact averaging of arbitrary detector-efficiency and dark-rate vectors at every outcome requires the average assignment matrix J_M/M. Since each permutation has M support entries while J_M/M has M^2 positive entries, at least M distinct permutation settings are necessary; cyclic shifts attain M. For K<M iid random permutations and a fixed eta vector in [0,1]^M, max_j |eta_hat_j-eta_bar| is at most sqrt(log(2M/delta)/(2K)) with probability at least 1-delta by Hoeffding and union bound, but no tomography stability transfer is proved.
assumptions: The hardware control is restricted to pure permutations of M outcome channels and exposure-weighted averaging.
Approximate random-setting bound fixes the detector vector independently of the random schedule; rows may be correlated across settings.
claims.status: Support-count lower bound and Hoeffding diagnostic derived. Approximate recovery with fewer settings remains unknown.
claims.novelty_boundary: Exact worst-case statement is elementary and restricted to permutation-only symmetrization; it is not an optical-design lower bound.
claims.costs: M settings for exact worst-case equalization; K settings give deviations of order sqrt(log(M/delta)/K) but require a missing heterogeneity-robust recovery theorem.
claims.falsifier: An exact averaging decomposition using fewer than M pure permutations or a control outside the stated class.

unknown: Priority and exact novelty of the combined complete-frame Poisson iid reduction plus state-independent anytime scalar calibration protocol.
Whether fewer random settings can retain the HLN phase-risk law under the resulting correlated heterogeneous row gains and dark offsets.
A direct full-device local minimax lower bound including residual outcomes in the background-dominated regime.
Transfer of pilot bounds across unbounded detector drift; palindrome cancellation only handles affine drift within one block.
Whether the fixed-N randomized-window schedule is available without source-rate-dependent detector gating, dead time, or saturation.
Known flux metrology accuracy, switch insertion loss and settling time, optical frame coefficient calibration, and finite-precision SDP/eigensolver cost.
Experimental validity of independent Poisson dark rates, stable detector-only efficiencies, and common row means after full outcome cycling.

finite_checks.result: Exact rational test on M=5 verifies cyclic averaging of nonuniform channel efficiencies/dark rates, state-independent total source efficiency, a fixed-setting state/gain confound, and small categorical one-global-total conditioning identities.
finite_checks.status: Finite algebra check only; it does not validate the uniform theorem, confidence-sequence stopping law, detector hardware, or optical synthesis.
